Chapter 1 of 11: The Bike in the Window

The Bike in the Window

Melissa was walking past the bike shop when she saw it: a shiny bike with a bell and a basket, sparkling in the window.

The price tag said $60. She didn't have $60, not even close.

Then a cheerful voice piped up: "Hi! I'm Azul! Want some help earning, saving, and learning your way to that bike?"

Chapter 1 of 11: The Bike in the Window

Needs vs. Wants

"Before we earn anything," said Azul, "let's get clear on something. A bike is fun, but you don't need it to stay healthy. That makes it a want. A warm coat, though? That's a need. Drag each thing below into the right box!"

Need
Want
Chapter 2 of 11: Earning Her First Coins

Earning Her First Coins

"Money doesn't just appear," Azul explained. "That's how your dad earns his: by doing something valuable at his job every day. Now let's earn your first coins! Tap each job to do it."

Tasks done: 0 / 5
Chapter 3 of 11: The Tricky Trade

The Tricky Trade

Melissa had 10 pink hair clips and really wanted her friend's stuffed unicorn. Drag the hair clips anywhere onto the square to offer a trade!

Chapter 4 of 11: The Invention of Money

The Invention of Money

"Even grown-ups study this stuff! People needed something everyone agreed was valuable and easy to trade," said Azul. Drag through history to see how money changed!

Seashells
Long ago, people traded seashells because everyone agreed they were rare and pretty.
Chapter 5 of 11: Tough Choices

Tough Choices

"Let's practice with $5 of birthday money," said Azul. A coloring book costs $5. A toy car also costs $5. Drag your $5 coin onto the ONE you want!

Chapter 6 of 11: What You Give Up

What You Give Up

"Here's a fancy idea," said Azul. "The opportunity cost isn't the $5 you spent. It's whatever you GAVE UP to get it. Tap to find out what you gave up."

Chapter 7 of 11: Setting Up the Lemonade Stand

Setting Up the Lemonade Stand

"Let's earn some SERIOUS money toward your bike," said Azul. Drag the price and watch how many customers show up!

Chapter 9 of 11: The Bank

The Bank

"A bank is like a safe, trusted house for your money, and it helps it grow a little too!" said Azul. "Let's deposit your Bike Fund and watch the weeks go by."

Tap to put your savings in the bank.
Chapter 10 of 11: Prices Creep Up

Prices Creep Up

"Here's a tricky one," said Azul. "Over time, the same dollar can buy less. Drag through the years and watch what happens to prices."

Grandpa's Day
A lollipop cost just 10 cents!
Uh oh, even the bike's price has crept up a little, from $60 to $63!
Chapter 11 of 11: The Big Lemonade Weekend

The Big Lemonade Weekend

"You know everything you need," said Azul. "Let's have your biggest lemonade weekend ever and finish your Bike Fund!"

You Did It!

Melissa rode off on her brand new bike, earned, saved, and grown, coin by coin. Along the way she learned about needs and wants, earning, trading, money, trade-offs, opportunity cost, supply and demand, saving, banking, and inflation.

Chapter 1 of 14: Every Nation, Its Own Money

Learning From Other Nations

"Before you can lead Starland's economy," says Azul, "you should learn how other nations handle their money. Almost every country has its own special currency!" Tap a flag, then tap its matching currency to connect them!

Chapter 2 of 14: What's an Exchange Rate?

How Much Is That, Really?

"As Starland's leader, you'll often need exchange rates when trading with other nations," Azul explains. An exchange rate tells you how much of one country's money equals another's. Right now, 1 US Dollar equals about 150 Japanese Yen. Drag the slider and watch!

💵
$1
=
💴
150 ¥
Try moving the slider. See how the Yen amount grows as you add more dollars? That's the exchange rate at work: it tells you exactly how much of one currency matches another.

Quick check: If 1 dollar equals 10 Mexican pesos, how many pesos is $3?

Chapter 3 of 14: Same Value, Different Price Tag

Bigger Numbers, Same Value!

"When Starland trades with other nations, the price tags will look very different, even for the same value," says Azul. A candy bar that costs $1 in the US might cost 14,000 rupiah in Indonesia. That's not 14,000 times more expensive, it's the SAME value, just counted in a currency with smaller units! Let's practice converting.

Round 1 of 3
Chapter 4 of 14: Strong or Weak? The Tug-of-War

The Currency Tug-of-War

"As Starland's leader, you'll watch this happen to YOUR currency," says Azul. Currencies are a little like a tug-of-war! When more people want to buy a currency, it gets stronger (this is called appreciation). When fewer people want it, it gets weaker (depreciation). Tap through the news events and watch the rope move!

⭐ Starland Star
Euro 🇪🇺
🟩
Chapter 5 of 14: What Makes a Currency Strong

Set Your Policies, Leader!

"Now it's time to set Starland's policies," says Azul. "Drag each bar as far as you like to decide how you'll run the country, and watch how it affects the Star's strength!"

Star Strength: Weak
Chapter 6 of 14: Understanding Inflation

What Really Drives Inflation?

"Inflation means prices rising over time," Azul explains. "As Starland's leader, two of your biggest tools affect it directly: how much money you print, and the interest rates you set. Drag them and watch what happens!"

💰 Money Printed A Little
🏦 Interest Rates Very Low
Inflation: Stable
Chapter 7 of 14: More Forces on Your Currency

The Control Room

"There's more to running Starland than we've covered," says Azul. "Jobs, foreign investors, and debt all pull on the Star too. Drag each one and watch the strength meter respond!"

💼 Employment (Jobs) Very Low
🌍 Foreign Investment Very Low
💳 Government Debt Very Low
Star Strength: Weak
Chapter 8 of 14: Growth and Confidence

What Investors Believe Matters Too

"Two more things move the Star," says Azul. "How fast Starland's economy is growing, and how confident investors FEEL about its future, even before anything actually happens! Drag each one and see."

📈 Economic Growth Very Slow
💭 Investor Confidence Very Low
Star Strength: Weak
Chapter 9 of 14: When Prices Spiral

When Money Loses Its Value FAST

"Leader, one warning," says Azul, growing serious. "If you ever print WAY too much money to solve a problem, prices can shoot up incredibly fast. This is called hyperinflation, and it can wreck an economy." Tap "Next Day" and watch what would happen to the price of a loaf of bread!

🍞

Who Wins When a Currency Changes?

"Meet two of Starland's citizens," says Azul: Sam, who sells toys to other countries, and Tara, who loves to travel abroad. When Starland's currency changes value, it isn't good or bad for everyone the same way!

Chapter 11 of 14: Trading With the World

Buying and Selling With Other Countries

"Starland sells LOTS of wheat to other countries," Azul explains. "To buy Starland's wheat, other countries need Starland's currency!" Tap the button and watch what happens.

Chapter 12 of 14: The Euro: One Money, Many Countries

Should Starland Share a Currency?

"Some day, neighboring nations might invite Starland to join a shared currency, like the Euro," says Azul. "Did you know 20 different European countries all share the SAME currency? Sharing a currency has good parts and tricky parts. Let's weigh them before you ever have to decide!" Read each statement and sort it!

Chapter 5 of 13: A Slice of the Orchard

Owning a Piece of Something Bigger

"See that big shared orchard over the hill?" Hazel points. "It's split into 10 equal slices. If you own a slice, you own a little piece of the WHOLE thing, and when the orchard grows, so does your slice. That's what a stock is."

Lend It, Don't Just Give It

"Sometimes neighbors need help buying young trees," Hazel says. "You could just GIVE them the money, or you could LEND it, and they promise to pay you back a little extra for the favor. That promise is called a bond."
